Overview
Some cars pass through owners like hire cars. Others become part of the family. This S8 falls firmly into the latter category.
Acquired by the vendor in October 2009, this V10-powered super-saloon has enjoyed 15 years of continuous, dedicated stewardship. That's a narrative of care you often don't find in this segment, where these cars can bounce between half a dozen keepers, each inheriting the previous owner's deferred maintenance. Not here. The stamped service book tells a different story entirely—one of consistent attention from Bedford Audi in the early years, transitioning to the same local garage for the last decade.
And what a sleeper this is: beneath that understated Daytona Grey exterior sits a 5.2-litre V10, its power channelled through a six-speed Tiptronic and quattro all-wheel drive. If there’s a better interpretation of the term ‘Q-car’ then we’ve not seen it.
This particular example wears its mileage honestly. The black leather interior with carbon fibre trim shows the expected signs of use—some wear to the driver's bolster and steering wheel—but the overall presentation speaks to an owner who cared. Bose surround sound, electric glass sunroof, rear privacy blinds: it's all present and correct. The vendor notes the left rear door blind needs attention, but that's the sort of minor niggle you'd expect after 15 years of actual use rather than garage-queen preservation.
What matters here isn't absolute perfection. It's provenance. And provenance like this doesn't come up often, which makes this V10-engined monster a potential bargain.

Summary
Fifteen years. One keeper. The same garage for the last decade. V10 S8s with this depth of ownership history are a rare thing.
This isn't a car that's been flipped between traders or left to languish with deferred maintenance. It's been a family member, with the service stamps to prove it. For the canny buyer who understands that provenance matters as much as performance, this represents a rare opportunity to acquire a V10 super-saloon that's been well looked-after rather than merely owned.
